comments.author: buu700
comments.story: Measuring progress toward AGI: A cognitive framework
comments.text: I wouldn't say consciousness is necessary or sufficient for AGI. If anything, that seems like quite an undesirable property to me. Wikipedia also makes a distinction between the two things: * [LINK] * [LINK] Imagine if we created the ultimate economic tool with the capacity to virtually end scarcity, only to find out that it was sentient and capable of suffering: [VIDEO] . That would be neat , but ultimately a huge letdown. Without the ethical freedom to take full advantage of it, it would remain more of a curiosity than anything. Well that's one perspective, anyway. I suppose consciousness could take many forms, and doesn't preclude the possibility that such an entity would have neutral – positive feelings about being tasked with massive amounts of labor 24/7. But it certainly simplifies things if we just don't have to worry about it.

comments.author: thesuperbigfrog
comments.story: Alexa is nagging you more because Amazon knows you don’t care about new features
comments.text: I have an Echo in my kitchen that I mainly use as a voice-activated timer and to play music or podcasts as I cook. I have noticed the behavior described in the article. I will set a timer and then Alexa will say "By the way did you know that I can blah blah blah? Do you want me to do it now?" To which I will answer "No". It is comically like the butter robot from Rick and Morty ( [VIDEO] ) in that I just want it to do a few simple tasks and it wants to be / do more.
